nodes.name: Forbidden pattern
nodes.statement: We say a tuple (a_1, dots, a_d) : (G^d)^d is a forbidden pattern with tip v : G^d if a_i, j = v_j for all i, j distinct. We also simply say (a_1, dots, a_d) is a forbidden pattern if it is a forbidden pattern with tip v for some v.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:forbidden-pattern}
  
  
  

  We say a tuple $(a_1, \dots, a_d) : (G^d)^d$ is a {\bf forbidden pattern with tip $v : G^d$} if
  $$a_{i, j} = v_j$$
  for all $i, j$ distinct. We also simply say $(a_1, \dots, a_d)$ is a {\bf forbidden pattern} if it is a forbidden pattern with tip $v$ for some $v$.

nodes.name: Multidimensional corner
nodes.statement: A multidimensional corner in d dimensions is a tuple of the form (x, x + ce_1, dots, x + ce_d) for some x : G^d and c : G, where ce_i is the vector of all zeroes except in position i where it is c. Such a corner is said to be trivial if c = 0.
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:multicorner}
  
  
  

  A {\bf multidimensional corner} in $d$ dimensions is a tuple of the form $(x, x + ce_1, \dots, x + ce_d)$ for some $x : G^d$ and $c : G$, where $ce_i$ is the vector of all zeroes except in position $i$ where it is $c$. Such a corner is said to be {\bf trivial} if $c = 0$.

nodes.label: def:multicorner

nodes.name: Corner-free number
nodes.statement: The d-dimensional corner-free number of G, denoted r_d(G) is the size of the largest set A in G^d such that A doesn't contain a non-trivial corner.

nodes.statement: Find A a corner-free set of density alpha = r_d(G)/N^d. If we pick m > dlog N/alpha translates of A randomly, then the expected number of elements not covered by any translate is N^d(1 - alpha)^m le exp(dN - malpha) < 1 Namely, there is some collection of m translates of A that covers all of G^d. Since being corner-free is translation-invariant, this cover by translates gives a coloring in m colors without non-trivial monochromatic corners. So chi_d(G) le m le 2d log N/alpha = 2d N^d log N/r_d(G) if we set eg m = floordlog N/alpha + 1.

Find $A$ a corner-free set of density $\alpha = r_d(G)/N^d$. If we pick $m > d\log N/\alpha$ translates of $A$ randomly, then the expected number of elements not covered by any translate is
  $$N^d(1 - \alpha)^m \le \exp(dN - m\alpha) < 1$$
  Namely, there is some collection of $m$ translates of $A$ that covers all of $G^d$. Since being corner-free is translation-invariant, this cover by translates gives a coloring in $m$ colors without non-trivial monochromatic corners. So
  $$\chi_d(G) \le m \le 2d \log N/\alpha = 2d N^d \log N/r_d(G)$$
  if we set eg $m = \floor{d\log N/\alpha} + 1$.

Since being corner-free is translation-invariant, this cover by translates gives a coloring in m colors without non-trivial monochromatic corners. nodes.name: Valid NOF protocol
nodes.statement: Given a function F : G^d to Bool, the NOF protocol P is valid in F at time t on input x if all participants correctly guess F(x), namely if guess_i(forget_i(x), broad(x, t)) = F(x) for all i : [d].
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:valid-protocol}
  
  
  

  Given a function $F : G^d \to \mathrm{Bool}$, the NOF protocol $P$ is {\bf valid in $F$ at time $t$ on input $x$} if all participants correctly guess $F(x)$, namely if
  $$\mathrm{guess}_i(\mathrm{forget}_i(x), \mathrm{broad}(x, t)) = F(x)$$
  for all $i : [d]$.
nodes.clean_text: Given a function F : G^d to Bool, the NOF protocol P is valid in F at time t on input x if all participants correctly guess F(x), namely if guess_i(forget_i(x), broad(x, t)) = F(x) for all i : [d].

nodes.statement: For all F, we define the trivial protocol by making participant i do "Send the t / d-th bit of the number of participant i + 1" and "Compute x_i from the binary representation given by participant i - 1, then compute F(x)".

nodes.name: Deterministic complexity of a protocol
nodes.statement: The communication complexity of a NOF protocol P for F is the smallest time t such that P is valid in F at time t on all inputs x, or infty if no such t exists.
